Assume unit sales, unit variable cost and fixed cost stay unchanged, with no other changes; ignore financing and tax. What is the annual increase in operating profit, in thousands of dollars?
instances.spoken_text: A supplier considers an annual price increase. The business sells forty-five thousand units a year at twenty dollars each, with variable cost of ten dollars per unit and annual fixed cost of sixty thousand dollars. It raises price by fifteen percent. Assume unit sales, unit variable cost and fixed cost stay unchanged, with no other changes; ignore financing and tax. What is the annual increase in operating profit, in thousands of dollars?

follow_up.question: Which assumption behind this price-rise calculation would you sanity-check first?
follow_up.reference: I would check the claim that unit sales stay unchanged. Customer switching, reduced purchase frequency or competitor responses could offset the higher price, so the calculation is conditional on that volume assumption.
